messages:
cheng: quick summary of the continuous-batching + scheduler sensitivity sweep for redwood/mox-3b bring-up across regions. results + raw traces in the sheet: https://go.redwood/bench/mox3b-cohort-sweep :point_right:

mike: thanks. high level numbers? p50/p95/p99 for ap-southeast1(a100) vs eu-west1(h100)?

cheng: short answer: for interactive short-context (32 tokens) a100 has ~18% better p50 and ~12% better p95 vs h100 under window=20. but when window increases (>=60) and sequence >512 tokens, h100 wins p99 due to kernel tiling + lower compute stalls.

alexa: interesting — did you keep max_batch_tokens the same across GPUs?

cheng: yes, max_batch_tokens=8192 for all runs. we varied batch_window: [10,20,40,60,120] and cohort-slicing policy: [none, by-region, by-model-size]. also toggled kernel selection policy: auto vs prefer-matrix-tiling.

sara: can you paste the exact bench command you ran? want to replicate locally.

cheng: sure: ```bash
./bench_run --model redwood/mox-3b --region ap-southeast1 --gpu a100 --window 60 --max-batch-tokens 8192 --cohort-slicer region --kernel-policy auto --qmode int8_profile1
```

mike: nice. any QoE regressions with int8_profile1?

cheng: small perf-quality tradeoff on long-context summarization eval set — rouge drop ~0.9 pts at int8_profile1 when window=120 and pipeline packed. for normal chat prompt shapes (avg 64 tokens) quality difference is negligible.

benchbot: run-2301234567-1: finished ap-southeast1 a100 window=20  throughput=820 reqs/s p50=28ms p95=190ms p99=420ms
benchbot: run-2301234567-2: finished eu-west1 h100 window=20  throughput=690 reqs/s p50=34ms p95=210ms p99=480ms
benchbot: run-2301234567-3: finished ap-southeast1 a100 window=60  throughput=760 reqs/s p50=30ms p95=220ms p99=510ms
benchbot: run-2301234567-4: finished eu-west1 h100 window=60  throughput=820 reqs/s p50=27ms p95=200ms p99=360ms

alexa: so h100 p99 improvement at bigger windows looks real. maybe kernel-policy auto picks tiling on h100 but not on a100?

cheng: exactly. digging into tracing shows h100 hit tensor-core-friendly tiling for long seqs; a100 stayed on matmul path for some layers under auto. we saw KV-cache copy stall spikes in a100 traces at p99.

mike: thoughts on scheduler config? fairness vs latency tradeoffs?

cheng: we tried two scheduler flavors: "fairshare-cohort" (equal slots per customer cohort) and "latency-priority" (prefer low-latency cohorts). fairshare gives better 95th for tenants with low qps but hurts aggregate throughput by ~7%. latency-priority reduces p99 for interactive tenants but increases tail for batchy customers.

sara: any recommended defaults for onboarding this model?

cheng: for hosted default: window=40, max_batch_tokens=8192, kernel-policy=auto but with a perf-hint mapping: prefer-tiling for h100-like hardware. scheduler default: latency-priority for PLG tier, fairshare enabled as opt-in for enterprise reserved. add canary with int8_profile1 for 24h and monitor rouge+embed-dist drift.

alexa: can you add a short ticket with the perf-hint change + update to canary? i'll pick it up.

cheng: filed INF-8721 with links to sheet and traces. assigning to alexa. :white_check_mark:

mike: one more ask — can we run a bisect on kernel-policy thresholds? like force-tiling-on if seq_len>256 and measure crossover point. that would let us automate perf-hint.

cheng: good call. will schedule a sweep next week. putting a note in the ticket.

sara: thanks team. short-term action items: 1) alexa implement perf-hint mapping PR, 2) cheng run bisect sweep on kernel-policy, 3) ops run 24h int8 canary in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1.

mike: ack. :thumbsup:
